userFeedback: V3基本可以，希望更加爆炸，特别是火焰和雷霆；保留此前材质感。
production: Original deterministic synthesis; no recordings, AI audio calls, downloaded samples or new dependencies.
runtimeIntegration: Offline audition revision only; game audio and all previous studies preserved.
listeningAcceptance: Pending audition of the new attack bodies; V3 received basic approval, not a device acceptance.

fire.userPreference: 2026-11-16: v3 is broadly acceptable; make fire/lightning more explosive while retaining natural material identity.
fire.provenance: Original deterministic NumPy/SciPy synthesis; no recordings, AI calls, external samples or downloads.

sourceChanges.ignition: Several brief, differently damped micro-fronts establish a 5-25ms contact instead of simply raising the old flame bed.
sourceChanges.body: Finite noise excites damped 146/229/347/493Hz pressure-volume modes, reinforced by a short 120-450Hz turbulent packet. No sub-bass sine/kick oscillator.
sourceChanges.expansion: Independent irregular packets expand over 70-250ms with changing bandwidth and non-repeating timing; the low-mid roll is separate from the ignition transient.
sourceChanges.tail: Sparse embers only, progressively weaker; no long constant white-noise wall or periodic flutter modulation.
sourceChanges.chargeAndWall: Gathering is modestly denser and still below impact. Wall uses a small one-off ignition and intermittent flame tongues, not a sequence of full explosions.

fire.mix: Local active-window energy controls ignition/body balance; final gain is only a safety cap at .64. Three variants independently change excitation, microtiming, modes and packet shapes.
fire.comparison: Assess v3/v4 at equal peak or matched loudness. Greater onset/body contrast is separate from overall playback loudness.
fire.acceptance: Numerical envelope/energy verification is not artistic or device listening acceptance.

thunder.direction: More explosive and full-bodied than v3, retaining a natural dry electric-arc identity.
thunder.provenance: Original deterministic NumPy/SciPy synthesis. No recordings, downloaded soundbanks, local AI or cloud generation.

structure.front: One 2–5ms broadband fracture with a small pressure impulse; the leading discharge remains strongest.
structure.body: A separate 20–100ms low-mid turbulent shock and rapidly damped non-harmonic structure modes, rather than merely a louder click.
structure.aftercracks: Two much quieter local cracks; neither a repeating gunfire train nor a sustained high hiss.
structure.tail: Body resolves within roughly 0.16 seconds; no long distant-thunder rumble.

thunder.differenceFromV3: v3 concentrated most single-hit energy in about 20ms. v4 adds independent short pressure and low-mid body sources so matching loudness still leaves a broader attack/body envelope.
thunder.network: Existing 0/.25/.50-second groups remain aligned. The later groups are subordinate and have less body than the main arc.
thunder.timing: Original .44/.44/1.10-second file lengths preserved; near-silent padding retains existing cue schedules.
thunder.variants: Three deterministic variants alter turbulent excitation, short damping and branch microtiming; no large pitch shifts.
thunder.mix: Peak cap 0.64 preserves headroom; no individual-cue loudness normalization. Root audition assembly matches loudness.
thunder.acceptance: Envelope and peak measurements are technical evidence only; explosive quality and realism remain pending human audition.

designNotes.physical: V3 physical source files are byte-identical; contact-to-preparation balance is reinforced by only 1.065x.

comparison.reference: PCM WAV; MP3 is a convenience preview and can shift gated loudness for sparse transients.
comparison.processing: Scalar gain only, no dynamics processor for matching.
comparison.schedule: Same v3 event onsets and sections; preparation remains bounded by release.
